# VAAET - Complete Documentation for AI Agent Consumption

Version: 3.0.0 | Date: 2026-03-08 | License: MIT

---

# 1. AGENTIC CONTEXT

## Project Identity

VAAET (Video Advanced Analysis of Traffic) is a computer vision system for analyzing vehicular traffic on the General Manuel Belgrano Bridge (Corrientes, Argentina). It detects, classifies, tracks, and estimates the speed of vehicles using SISE surveillance camera footage.

### Three-Module Pipeline (ADR-009)
- Module 0 — Bootstrap (archived): archive/00_bootstrap/01_legacy_collection.ipynb — Historical YOLO 11 + OpenCV + SORT pipeline that generated the original traffic_data table. NEVER runs again.
- Module 1 — Data Preparation: notebooks/01_data_prep/data_preparation.ipynb — One-time feature engineering + auto-labeling + SMOTE + MLP training. Exports .keras and .joblib artifacts.
- Module 2 — Production: notebooks/02_production/traffic_analyzer.ipynb — YOLO 11 + SORT + speed estimation + trained MLP classifier + DB persistence + self-improving feedback loop.
- Shared code: src/ — Reusable Python modules (config, db, features, labeling, perception) imported by Modules 1 and 2.
- Runtime: Google Colab (free GPU). NO servers, REST APIs, microservices, or containers.
- Persistence: PostgreSQL on AWS RDS (optional). 3 tables: traffic_data (legacy), telemetry_raw + traffic_classifications (active).

### Technology Stack
- Object detection: YOLO 11 (Ultralytics) — 5 variants by video duration
- Computer vision: OpenCV — video I/O, optical flow, annotations
- Numerical: NumPy — vectorized operations, statistics
- ML (speed smoothing): scikit-learn MLPRegressor — NOT a real CNN
- Traffic classification: TensorFlow/Keras — MLP Sequential (evolvable to LSTM)
- Data analysis: Pandas + SQLAlchemy — feature engineering and persistence
- Class balancing: imbalanced-learn SMOTE — synthetic oversampling
- Database: PostgreSQL via psycopg2-binary / SQLAlchemy (AWS RDS)

## Architectural Boundaries

1. Module 0 is FROZEN — never modify archive/00_bootstrap/01_legacy_collection.ipynb
2. src/config.py is the SINGLE source of truth for constants, thresholds, and paths
3. src/db.py is the SINGLE point of DB configuration — credentials via environment variables only
4. Speed fusion is 70% physics + 30% MLP — do not alter without experimental evidence
5. is_stationary() criteria use AND-conjunction — do not relax to OR without ADR
6. Video filename format is strict: bridge_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS_to_HH-MM-SS.mp4
7. Tables telemetry_raw and traffic_classifications require ADR-008 — do not modify schema without new ADR
8. 14 features are canonical — defined in src/config.py:FEATURE_COLS
9. 4 traffic states: Normal (0), Reduced (1), Congested (2), Accident (3) — defined in src/config.py:STATE_LABELS
10. Shared src/ modules must remain notebook-importable — no CLI entrypoints

## Always / Ask / Never

Always: Fix syntax errors, update docstrings, add type hints, add markdown cells, format code PEP 8, fix config inconsistencies, update AGENTS.md when structure changes.

Ask: Change calibration parameters, modify speed calculation or is_stationary(), add dependencies, change DB schema, modify YOLO model selection, refactorings >20% of a module, change auto-labeling thresholds, modify MLP/LSTM architecture.

Never: Hardcode AWS credentials, modify Module 0 notebook, delete test_sistema() or synthetic demos, modify traffic_data without ADR, break Colab Free compatibility, commit .pt files, print credentials, modify telemetry_raw or traffic_classifications without ADR, remove HITL fields, commit .keras/.joblib or processed CSVs.

---

# 2. PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS (PRD)

## Implemented Requirements

1. Video loading: Only accepts bridge_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS_to_HH-MM-SS.mp4
2. Automatic YOLO 11 selection: <1h:x, 1-3h:l, 3-6h:m, 6-12h:s, >12h:n
3. Optional persistence: PostgreSQL AWS RDS, data every minute, no hardcoded credentials
4. Hybrid speed calculation: Physics + Optical Flow + MLP, with limits and stationary exclusion
5. Multi-camera: Automatic layout detection (1, 2, 4 views)
6. Perspective: Calibratable homographies, optional external loading
7. Persistent tracking: Lightweight SORT with robust IDs
8. Historical values: Recent averages when no detections
9. Auto-download: Processed video with overlays
10. Colab optimization: Frame skipping, memory cleanup
11. Modularity: Shared src/ modules with high cohesion, low coupling
12. Clear outputs: Success/error messages with emoji prefixes
13. Traffic state classification: 4 states (Normal, Reduced, Congested, Accident) with TF/Keras MLP

## Use Cases

SISE operational monitoring, traffic engineering, urban planning, academic research, emergency management.

---

# 3. SOFTWARE DESIGN (DDS)

## Architecture

Three-module pipeline with shared src/ modules. Module 0 (Bootstrap) generated historical data and is now archived. Module 1 (Data Preparation) trains the traffic classifier. Module 2 (Production) runs the full perception + classification pipeline.

## Components

### 3.1 Detection and Recognition (src/perception/detector.py)
Frame BGR -> Ultralytics YOLO 11 inference -> NMS (IoU=0.4, conf=0.5) -> List of (bbox, class, confidence)

### 3.2 Speed Calculation (src/perception/speed.py)
History deque 30 frames -> Optical Flow Lucas-Kanade (camera compensation) -> Euclidean displacement -> Perspective correction (factor by Y: near=1.8, mid=1.0, far=0.6) -> Physics speed (px->m->km/h) -> Fusion: 0.7*physics + 0.3*MLP -> Plausibility filter [2, 120] km/h -> Temporal smoothing

### 3.3 Stationary Detection
Requires ALL (AND): >=200 frames, displacement<5px, segment<3px, std<2.5px, avg_frame<0.3px, max_frame<1.5px

### 3.4 Feature Engineering (src/features.py)
9 raw telemetry fields -> 14 features: avg_speed, total_vehicles, count_car, count_truck, count_bus, count_motorcycle, count_bicycle, heavy_vehicle_ratio, delta_speed, delta_count, transition_flag, speed_variance, hour_of_day, weather_condition

### 3.5 Traffic State Classifier (Module 1)
Model: TF/Keras Sequential MLP — Input(14) -> Dense(64,relu) -> BatchNorm -> Dropout(0.3) -> Dense(32,relu) -> BatchNorm -> Dropout(0.2) -> Dense(n_classes,softmax).
Compile: optimizer=adam, loss=sparse_categorical_crossentropy, metrics=accuracy.
Callbacks: EarlyStopping(patience=15, restore_best_weights), ReduceLROnPlateau(patience=5, factor=0.5).
Auto-labeling (src/labeling.py): Normal (avg_speed>40, total_vehicles<15), Reduced (10<=speed<=40 and 15<=vehicles<=25), Congested (speed<5, vehicles>25, 2+ consecutive), Accident (speed~0, delta_speed<-20, 3+ consecutive).

## Database Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE traffic_data (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  clip_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  record_time TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  avg_speed NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL,
  count_car INTEGER NOT NULL,
  count_truck INTEGER NOT NULL,
  count_bus INTEGER NOT NULL,
  count_motorcycle INTEGER NOT NULL,
  count_bicycle INTEGER NOT NULL,
  total_vehicles INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (clip_id, record_time)
);

CREATE TABLE telemetry_raw (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  source_record_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES traffic_data(id),
  clip_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  record_time TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  avg_speed NUMERIC(5,2), total_vehicles INTEGER,
  count_car INTEGER, count_truck INTEGER, count_bus INTEGER,
  count_motorcycle INTEGER, count_bicycle INTEGER,
  heavy_vehicle_ratio NUMERIC(5,4), delta_speed NUMERIC(6,2),
  delta_count INTEGER, transition_flag SMALLINT,
  speed_variance NUMERIC(8,4), hour_of_day INTEGER,
  weather_condition SMALLINT DEFAULT 0,
  ingested_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE traffic_classifications (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  telemetry_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_raw(id),
  model_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  predicted_state SMALLINT NOT NULL,
  confidence NUMERIC(5,4),
  human_override_state SMALLINT,
  human_override_by TEXT,
  human_override_at TIMESTAMP,
  classified_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

FK chain: traffic_classifications -> telemetry_raw -> traffic_data.
HITL fields: human_override_state, human_override_by, human_override_at (designed for Module 2 feedback loop).

---

# 4. ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS (ADRs)

## ADR-001: Monolithic Notebook (Superseded by ADR-009)
Decision: All code in vaaet.ipynb for Colab portability. Now replaced by modular src/ architecture.

## ADR-002: Adaptive YOLO 11 (Superseded by ADR-009)
Decision: 5 variants by duration (<1h:x, 1-3:l, 3-6:m, 6-12:s, >12:n). Logic now in src/perception/detector.py.

## ADR-003: SORT over DeepSORT (Superseded by ADR-009)
Decision: Matching by Euclidean distance (100px) without visual ReID. Logic now in src/perception/tracker.py.

## ADR-004: MLP as Smoother (Superseded by ADR-009)
Decision: MLPRegressor(64,32) trained with random data, fusion 70/30. Does not improve real accuracy, acts as stochastic regularizer. The "CNN" name in legacy code is incorrect.

## ADR-005: PostgreSQL AWS RDS (Superseded by ADR-009)
Decision: Remote persistence to survive ephemeral Colab sessions. Logic now in src/db.py.

## ADR-006: Ultra-Conservative Stationary Detection (Superseded by ADR-009)
Decision: AND-conjunction of 6 statistical criteria. High precision, limited recall for micro-moving vehicles.

## ADR-007: Google Colab as Runtime (Superseded by ADR-009)
Decision: Free GPU, zero config, portability. No CI/CD, ephemeral sessions.

## ADR-008: TensorFlow/Keras Traffic Classifier (Active)
Decision: MLP Sequential (Dense 64->32->n_classes) with auto-labeling + SMOTE. 2 new tables (telemetry_raw, traffic_classifications) with FK to traffic_data. 4 states: Normal(0), Reduced(1), Congested(2), Accident(3). HITL fields for future human correction.

## ADR-009: Modular Three-Stage Architecture (Active)
Decision: Replace monolithic notebook with three-module pipeline + shared src/ code. Module 0 archived, Module 1 for data prep, Module 2 for production. Follows SOLID, KISS, YAGNI principles.

# 5. KPIs

| KPI | Metric | Target | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detection/Classification | F1-Score | 97% | Declared target, no real benchmark measured |
| Speed | MAE | < 5 km/h | Declared target, no ground truth available |
| Tracking | ID Switches | Minimize | No formal measurement |
| Processing | FPS | Variable by model | No published benchmark |
| Stationary | Classification precision | High | No quantitative evaluation |
| Traffic classification | F1-macro | >= 0.85 | Pending training with real data |
| Accident recall | Recall class 3 | >= 0.90 | Pending training with real data |

Validation guide Module 1: Cell 7 generates classification_report + confusion matrix. F1-macro >= 0.85 required. Accident recall >= 0.90 critical.

---

# 6. DATA LINEAGE

Source: SISE cameras on Belgrano Bridge, MP4 video.

## Module 0 — Bootstrap (archived)
Pipeline: Video -> Frames 30fps -> YOLO detections -> SORT tracks -> Hybrid speed -> Aggregation/minute -> PostgreSQL.
MLP speed smoother: Trained with random data (scaffold). No speed ground truth.
Output: Annotated .mp4 video + records in traffic_data.

## Module 1 — Data Preparation
Pipeline: traffic_data (SQL) -> DataFrame -> Feature Engineering (9->14 cols) -> Auto-Labeling (4 states) -> SMOTE -> StandardScaler -> MLP Training -> Evaluation -> Export (.keras, .joblib) -> Persistence (telemetry_raw + traffic_classifications).
14 features: avg_speed, total_vehicles, count_car, count_truck, count_bus, count_motorcycle, count_bicycle, heavy_vehicle_ratio (truck+bus/total), delta_speed (diff t-1), delta_count (diff t-1), transition_flag (delta_speed>10 and delta_count>5), speed_variance (rolling 5), hour_of_day, weather_condition (nocturnal=1).
Artifacts: traffic_classifier.keras, feature_scaler.joblib, label_mapping.joblib in models/intelligence/.

## Module 2 — Production
Pipeline: Video -> YOLO + SORT + speed estimation -> Telemetry per minute -> Feature Engineering -> MLP Classifier inference -> Classification persistence -> Optional HITL feedback -> Retraining.
Uses trained artifacts from Module 1. Persists to telemetry_raw and traffic_classifications.

Privacy: Videos may contain license plates. No frames are stored, only per-minute aggregates.

---

# 7. BIASES AND LIMITATIONS

- COCO bias: YOLO trained on COCO, possible under-representation of bicycles and motorcycles
- No adverse condition evaluation: rain, fog, night, backlight
- Speed without ground truth: pixel->meter conversion manually calibrated
- MLP speed smoother trained with random data: does not improve real accuracy
- Tracking without ReID: loses identity in occlusions >1 second
- Ephemeral Colab: max 12h sessions, GPU not guaranteed, no automatic retry
- Auto-labeling inherits Module 0 biases: if YOLO fails, state labels are incorrect
- Accident class under-represented (~2%): SMOTE partially mitigates, may generate synthetic artifacts
- No temporality: MLP does not capture sequences, future evolution to LSTM
- Simulated weather: weather_condition=0 constant until meteorological API integration

---

# 8. DOMAIN CONTEXT

- Bridge: General Manuel Belgrano, 1700m length, 8.3m roadway width
- Cameras: SISE dynamic cameras at 60m height, zoom, pan, night vision
- Vehicle types: car, truck, bus, motorcycle, bicycle
- Typical speeds: 40-80 km/h normal flow, 0-20 km/h congestion
- Persistence: 1 record/minute with average speed and counts by type
- Traffic states: Normal (0), Reduced (1), Congested (2), Accident (3)
- Features: 14 engineered columns from 9 raw telemetry fields
